title: Best SEO Strategies for Small Businesses in 2026
summary: Effective SEO strategies allow small businesses to reach their target audiences via search engines, whether that’s local shoppers or a niche market.
body_markdown:
SEO strategies for small businesses aim to help stores show up at the top of results when shoppers search for related topics. These strategies include researching the keywords customers use, optimizing website content, maintaining a local business listing, and earning links from other websites.


The audience is there. People shop more than a[billion times a day](https://blog.google/products/ads-commerce/ai-personalization-and-the-future-of-shopping/) on Google alone. According to Google, consumers say they used the search engine or YouTube in about two-thirds of purchases where they discovered a new brand, product, or retailer.


Here’s how search engine optimization works for a small business, how to apply these strategies to your website, and what it looks like in practice for ecommerce brands.


## Benefits of SEO strategies for small businesses


Search engine optimization (SEO) is the practice of improving your website so it shows up at the top of[search engine results pages (SERPs)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/serp) . SEO is an organic marketing tactic; compared to paid campaigns, which reach only the shoppers you pay to reach and stop the moment the budget runs out, search-optimized pages keep attracting traffic to your site for as long as those pages stay relevant.


For example, the automotive accessories retailer[Boost Auto](http://boostautoparts.com/) grew their $5,000 investment into millions in annual revenue on that principle. “We spend next to nothing on advertising, like less than 1% of our revenue,” Founder and CEO Adam Wolfe says in a[Shopify case study](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/boost-auto) . “Everything we do is native marketing. We’ve never hired an SEO agency. We use Shopify, read a couple articles, and we are the number one in search for most of what we want.”


Rank higher on Google


Use this free SEO checklist to optimize your website and content. Learn how to rank for relevant search terms so more shoppers discover your store first.


[Download checklist](https://www.shopify.com/first-sale/seo-checklist)


## SEO strategies for small businesses


- Match keywords to search intent
- Optimize your product and collection pages
- Build local search visibility with a Google Business Profile
- Strengthen internal links and earn backlinks
- Prepare your site for AI search


Here’s how to put five small business SEO strategies to work:


### Match keywords to search intent


[Keyword research](https://www.shopify.com/blog/keyword-research) is the process of finding the words and phrases people type into search engines when they look for products like yours. Search intent is the goal behind the phrases they use: a shopper might search “leather tote” to browse products, “leather tote care” for instructions, and “durable tote bags” to research and compare. Knowing the phrases shoppers use and the intent behind them can tell you what kind of website pages to build.


“Sometimes if you don’t have direction, you’ll write a blog, and it’ll be a great blog, but no one’s actually searching for that,” says JJ Follano, cofounder of the sustainable-goods marketplace[Zero Waste Store](https://zerowastestore.com/) , on the[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/zero-waste-store-sustainability-seo-growth) podcast. Before writing, JJ researches keywords and topic ideas to confirm search demand exists.


“Aligning intent with content is the whole point—otherwise you won’t rank,” says Kyle Risley, senior lead of SEO at Shopify. “Type the keyword into Google and scrutinize the results. Are you seeing mostly product pages? Then target the query with a product page. All informational articles and guides? Target that query with a blog post.”


Free tools can help you with your research.[Google Keyword Planner](https://business.google.com/en-all/ad-tools/keyword-planner/) shows how often terms get searched.[Google Search Console](https://www.shopify.com/blog/google-search-console) shows the queries your site already appears for.


Within your list, Kyle recommends prioritizing long-tail keywords, or the specific, lower-volume phrases larger competitors skip. A small pet supply store, for example, may not be able to rank for a high-volume query like “dog beds,” but it can rank for one like “what kind of bed does a golden retriever need?”


### Optimize your product and collection pages


[On-page SEO](https://www.shopify.com/blog/on-page-seo) is the work of making each page on your site easy for search engines to understand. Google assembles your search listing from your page: The page title typically becomes the clickable headline, and the snippet below it draws on the page’s visible text (or, at times, your meta description). In Shopify, you can edit each page’s title, meta description, and URL in the search engine listing section.


Matthew Burroughs, founder of the plant retailer[Plant Material](https://plant-material.com/) , credits the store’s visibility in search results to his wife, Heather, who has managed its page titles, descriptions, and other meta tags in Shopify since their online store launched. “We’ve been really focused on that since day one, so that we would pop up and could compete without a lot of ad dollars,” Matthew says on the[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/plant-material-inventory-management-advice) podcast.


Kyle Risley recommends naming pages with the language a shopper would use to search. “If you are selling red t-shirts, calling the collection ‘Red’ won’t help you turn up in SEO,” he says. “You’d want to call it ‘Red T-shirts’ to show up in search results.”


Similar thinking applies to the number of collections you create. “Let’s say you sell spices. There are probably 20 to 30 different ways you can organize those spices,” Kyle says. “You should create pages for each category: Indian spices, Italian spices, barbecue spices. There’s a lot of buyer intent there.”


Shopify generates sitemaps, canonical tags, and product structured data (the technical SEO signals that help search engines index and display a site) for every store. Themes are built to be mobile-friendly, which matters because of[Google’s mobile-first indexing](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/mobile/mobile-sites-mobile-first-indexing) . Google reads the mobile version of your site, not its desktop version, when determining what to rank.


### Build local search visibility with a Google Business Profile


[Local SEO](https://www.shopify.com/blog/local-seo-retail) is the practice of optimizing your online presence to attract customers who are searching in your area. It’s relevant to any business with a physical location or service area.


[Google ranks local results](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091) on three factors: relevance, distance, and prominence. It recommends that businesses provide complete, detailed information for the best chances of being matched to local searches. By creating a free[Google Business Profile](https://www.shopify.com/blog/google-business-profile) , you can put your business name, hours, and location in front of local customers on both Search and Maps.


[Google says](https://services.google.com/fh/files/helpcenter/1_services_gbp_best_practices_playbook_2026.pdf) that businesses with complete profiles get seven times more clicks, and adding photos brings 42% more requests for directions. Google draws on your review count and score to gauge prominence, so keep your listings consistent across online directories and respond to reviews as they come in.


### Strengthen internal links and earn backlinks


[Internal links](https://www.shopify.com/blog/internal-links-seo) connect pages within your own website, while[backlinks](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-are-backlinks-in-seo-why-backlinks-still-matter) are links from other websites to yours. Both help search engines find your pages and understand how they relate. Internal links do double duty; the same paths that help shoppers navigate your site are the same paths search engines crawl to discover it.


“Think about how you would like pages to be linked together—think about users and accessibility over links for SEO,” says Arthur Camberlein, tech SEO lead at Shopify. “If you have a blog post talking about helmets, you should create links to several helmet products, categories, and related accessories, like gloves.” Connect blog posts to the products they mention, and link every collection from your main navigation.


For backlinks, consider where you already have relationships, such as suppliers who list their stockists or community organizations you sponsor. Skip any shortcuts.[Google’s spam policies](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/essentials/spam-policies) treat links exchanged for money, goods, or services as grounds to rank a site lower.


### Prepare your site for AI search


[AI search optimization](https://www.shopify.com/blog/aeo-for-ecommerce) means making your business findable to AI assistants that answer shopping questions. This includes standalone assistants like ChatGPT and Claude, as well as those built into search engines, like Google’s AI Overviews and AI Mode.


The channel, while still modest compared to traditional search, is growing. AI-driven traffic to retail sites grew 693% year over year during the 2025 holiday season,[according to Adobe research](https://business.adobe.com/blog/ai-driven-traffic-surges-across-industries) , and visitors converted 31% more often than those arriving from other traffic sources.


The fundamentals of AI search overlap with traditional SEO tactics. In addition to SEO best practices, write product pages that read like answers. Write about materials, dimensions, and use cases in clear, factual language that an assistant can directly quote when a shopper asks.


Beyond that, showing up in AI searches is less a separate optimization project than making sure your pages are available when an AI assistant assembles its answer.[According to Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) , there are no additional requirements to appear in its AI Overviews or AI Mode; pages that are indexed and eligible for snippets are also cited by its AI features, and if your store ranks in regular search results, it’s already eligible to appear.


Similarly,[OpenAI says](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11128490-shopping-with-chatgpt-search) ChatGPT’s product results are organic, selected from structured metadata like price and product descriptions. Detailed, factual product pages serve your search rankings and give AI assistants material to draw on.


## SEO for small businesses FAQ


### What are some effective SEO strategies for small businesses?


Effective small business SEO strategies include matching keywords to search intent, writing descriptive page titles and meta descriptions, and creating a Google Business Profile to improve local search rankings. Internal linking and backlinks from local directories and news sites build authority over time. Track SEO performance in Google Search Console and Google Analytics, then prioritize refining the pages that already bring in organic traffic and sales.


### What is the 80/20 rule in SEO?


The[80/20 rule](https://www.shopify.com/blog/80-20-rule) is that roughly 80% of results come from 20% of causes. This is an application of the Pareto principle, not a literal measurement. In small business SEO, it means a small share of your pages and target keywords drives most of your search traffic. Reviewing your traffic data shows you where to focus your SEO efforts.


### What are the top 5 SEO strategies?


Top strategies for a small business’s SEO program include matching relevant keywords to search intent, optimizing product and collection pages, creating a Google Business Profile to attract local customers, building internal links and backlinks, and writing in a way that benefits AI search. Your SEO strategy depends on your business; a retailer with a physical storefront may start with local search, while an ecommerce-only brand may start with keyword research.
